summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes and request timeouts tied to continuous batching behavior
description: Issue summary: Since ~2026-02-20 02:00 UTC BrightCart is seeing elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent request timeouts for text-generation requests routed to redwood-7b-v2. Impact: customer reports production timeouts for inference calls (client-observed 504/timeout errors) and increased tail latency impacting SLAs. Environment: BrightCart on dedicated cluster in us-east; requests route through API gateway to serving-runtime with continuous batching enabled. Observed start time: ~2026-02-20 02:00 UTC; change window: a scheduler rollout was applied 2026-02-20 01:45 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of single-turn chat/generation requests (avg tokens per request ~120) to BrightCart tenant on redwood-7b-v2 in us-east.
2) Observe p95/p99 latency over 5-10 minute windows via /metrics or Console per-route dashboard.
3) Under the impacted scheduler config, tail latency spikes to >1.5s p95 and >3s p99 with intermittent 504s.
logs_and_metrics: Gateway logs show increased 504 responses correlated with serving-runtime 10s timeouts (HTTP 504 from api-gateway) between 02:00-03:30 UTC.

Serving runtime traces show longer batch build times and larger effective batch sizes during spike windows; continuous_batching.max_delay_ms observed at 50ms for affected hosts (changed from 20ms in recent rollout).
Prometheus: redwood_request_duration_seconds p99 jumped from ~380ms to ~2.1s for route 'brightcart-prod-gen' starting 02:00 UTC.
KV cache hit-rate unchanged; CPU/GPU utilization remained within normal bounds but observed increased variance in batch assembly time on GPU nodes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Scheduler rollout increased continuous_batching.max_delay_ms to 50ms which increases wait window and yields larger, uneven batches causing higher tail latency for single-request bursts.

Hypothesis 2: A packing heuristic change in the serving-runtime interacts poorly with redwood-7b-v2 attention kernel for certain sequence-length distributions, producing longer kernel selects and blocking in the batch assembly path.
We reproduced locally by toggling max_delay_ms between 20 and 50ms; 50ms reproduces p99 spikes consistent with production.
Related change: platform PR #8421 adjusted scheduler backoff and batching defaults; flagged for rollback verification.
Traces show some batches with head-of-line requests waiting for additional requests to hit the batch window, increasing per-request latency for low-concurrency bursts.
customer_communication: 2026-02-20 03:05 UTC - Support (Priya): 'We are investigating elevated p95/p99 latency and timeouts for your inference calls. Temporary mitigation is being applied.'
2026-02-20 04:12 UTC - Support (Marco): 'We have reduced continuous_batching.max_delay_ms from 50ms -> 15ms for your tenant as a mitigation. Please confirm if you see improvement.'
2026-02-20 04:25 UTC - Customer (BrightCart Ops): 'We see immediate reduction in observed timeouts and p99 dropped under 700ms. Monitoring for regressions.'
mitigation_applied: 2026-02-20 04:10 UTC - Temporary config override applied: continuous_batching.max_delay_ms=15ms for BrightCart dedicated pool (targeted hosts) to prioritize latency over batching efficiency.
Traffic routing adjusted to favor low-latency nodes in us-east for BrightCart until fix is rolled out.
Added alert on batch assembly time > 30ms to detect recurrence.
next_steps: 1) Roll back scheduler change in PR #8421 for a canary subset and verify p99 behavior (owner: Marco).
2) Add model-specific batching profile for redwood-7b-v2 to limit batch wait for typical sequence-lengths (owner: Serving Runtime team).
3) Update continuous-batching runbook with guidance for max_delay_ms defaults and tenant overrides (owner: SRE).
4) Longer-term: evaluate adaptive batching heuristics that consider request arrival distribution and sequence-length to avoid H-O-L latency.
